fe63fffe3e.q: How does Section 232 tariff implementation affect solar project backlogs and earnings?
fe63fffe3e.a: When Section 232 impacts module availability or pricing, projects don't get built if modules aren't secured or prices rise 15-20 cents, making projects no longer pencil financially until power purchase agreement prices increase. This means suppliers sit on manufactured inventory, labor doesn't deploy to sites, and EPCs struggle to fill capacity, all of which hits earnings in Q1, Q2, and Q3.

3ca033e146.q: What provisions in the bipartisan permitting bill specifically benefit solar projects with large load customers?
3ca033e146.a: If selling energy to a data center over 20 megawatts, the bill requires the large load (data center) to pay for infrastructure buildout costs to the grid, shifting interconnection upgrade costs away from the solar developer. For behind-the-meter projects, the bring your own capacity concept allows large loads to come with their project in hand, reducing utility interconnection delays.

72e9538841.q: Why does the Democratic House majority mean the permitting bill must pass in lame duck or not at all?
72e9538841.a: The current permitting bill reflects Republican priorities and is designed to give the president power for oil and gas projects over the next two years. A Democratic House with 252 seats and 55-seat Democratic Senate would write a completely different permitting bill, so this version will not pass under Democratic control—making the lame duck session the final window.

3ab163df3b.q: What metrics should investors examine beyond backlog when evaluating solar equipment company earnings?
3ab163df3b.a: Examine the definition of backlog itself—whether it is awarded, verbal, written, or ready to manufacture—as companies report this differently. Look at quarterly changes in adjusted operating expenses to see if a CEO is investing in growth or tightening operations. Track customer concentration percentages in SEC filings to detect if major customers are being lost, trends not always discussed on earnings calls.

4b0d721a98.q: How are large data centers and tech companies changing solar deployment models in the United States?
4b0d721a98.a: Google acquired Intersect Power, one of the largest solar IPPs, and SB Energy (SoftBank's solar arm) is pursuing an IPO as a powered land developer and data center developer. Large loads view solar favorably because of its cost, lack of fuel price variability, and speed to grid. Solar companies have become skilled at community development and can deploy smaller community solar or large-scale solar where communities are open to it.
